# Duna — Style Reference

> Oil-paint meadow hung on a white gallery wall, one lime seed. GT America at weight 400 on paper-white, warm-stone panels and pill-shaped ink buttons, with a single lime dot as the only signal inside the interface.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Duna speaks a painted-pastoral compliance language. A white canvas #ffffff carries almost everything, warm off-white panels hold quotes and product cards (Linen Surface #f7f7f5 and Stone Surface #edece7), and a frosted #ffffffe6 layer floats chips over imagery. The chromatic budget inside the interface is two hues, and both are rationed to dots: teal #45848d marks capability tags and lime #aeec1d marks a single "AI era" signal. Every other saturated pigment lives inside the painted landscapes and blurred gradient fields, which are decorative and not tokens. Typography is one family, GT America, held at weight 400 from 12px to 72px, with tracking that tightens to -0.06em at the hero. Size and negative tracking carry hierarchy rather than weight, and only the 80px stat numerals step up to 500. Shape is pill-and-soft, with 999px on actions and tags and 24px on cards. Elevation is nearly absent: two shadows exist on the whole page. The overall effect reads as a gallery wall for a regulated product rather than a dashboard selling one.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Page body, logo marquee band, stat and feature sections, and text on dark imagery (33 text uses). The white gallery wall gives the paintings room to carry all the color. |
| Linen Surface | `#f7f7f5` | `--color-linen-surface` | Testimonial quote panel, quiet secondary blocks and inset tiles (5 uses). It is one tonal step off white, so a container reads without a border or shadow. |
| Stone Surface | `#edece7` | `--color-stone-surface` | Product cards, the image-placeholder ground and hairline dividers between feature columns (10 uses, the most frequent fill). A warm grey keeps the canvas mineral rather than clinical. |
| Frosted Glass | `#ffffffe6` | `--color-frosted-glass` | Floating capability tags over gradient fields and overlay chips on imagery (8 uses). At 90% white, painted color bleeds through without hurting legibility. |
| Plum Veil | `#1b062499` | `--color-plum-veil` | Hero announcement badge fill and muted plum text on light ground (6 uses). This is the aubergine ink at 60%, so it tints with the painting instead of covering it. |
| Ember Ink | `#160f0c` | `--color-ember-ink` | Every "Schedule a demo" pill fill, the inverted surface. This is the only filled action color, a near-black with a brown undertone that matches the warm canvas. Do not use it for headline text. |
| Jet Figure | `#000000` | `--color-jet-figure` | The 80px stat numerals and the product-section H2 (13 uses). Pure black is reserved for numbers that must land hardest on the page. |
| Plum Ink | `#1b0624` | `--color-plum-ink` | Section H2s, stat labels and feature titles (19 uses). The signature headline ink is an aubergine near-black, so hierarchy carries a faint hue that grey type would lack. |
| Graphite Ink | `#292421` | `--color-graphite-ink` | Nav links, body paragraphs and the hero H1, which measures #222221 and snaps here as a non-token value (19 uses). This is the warm workhorse reading tone. |
| Ash Caption | `#4d4846` | `--color-ash-caption` | Feature descriptions, hero lede and testimonial attribution titles (9 uses). It steps body copy back one level while keeping the warm brown cast. |
| Fog Caption | `#898683` | `--color-fog-caption` | "Built for businesses where compliance matters" eyebrow, marquee captions and metadata (6 uses). This is the quietest legible text and stays reserved for labels. |
| Lagoon Pulse | `#45848d` | `--color-lagoon-pulse` | 6px status dots inside floating capability tags (8 uses, plus a #46838c near-duplicate that is not a token). The teal echoes the painted water. Do not promote it to a button fill. |
| Keylime Signal | `#aeec1d` | `--color-keylime-signal` | The single dot in the "Built for the AI era" chip (1 use). It is the brightest pixel in the UI layer, which is why there is only one. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |

## Tokens — Typography

### GT America — the only voice, held at weight 400 from caption to hero · `--font-gt-america`

- **Substitute:** Inter Tight at 400, Geist at 400, Instrument Sans at 400. GT America Standard Regular draws true to its weight and slightly sturdier than Inter at the same number, so do not drop substitutes to 300. For the 80px stat numerals, use Inter Tight at 500 with `tnum` enabled.
- **Weights:** 400, 500. The cut named "GT America Medium" is declared at 400 but renders as a medium stroke, so treat it as 500 visually.
- **Sizes:** 12px, 13px, 14px, 16px, 17px, 18px, 20px, 22px, 24px, 40px, 44px, 72px, 80px
- **Line height:** 1.0 at 72px and 80px, 1.1 at 44px, 1.2 at 40px, 1.3 at 12px, 1.4 at 13px, 20px and 24px, 1.5 at 14px and 16px
- **Letter spacing:** -4.32px at 72px (-0.06em), -2.2px at 44px (-0.05em), -1.2px at 40px (-0.03em), -0.72px at 24px (-0.03em), -0.4px at 20px (-0.02em), -0.16px at 16px (-0.01em), 0 at 13px, 14px and 80px, +0.24px at 12px (+0.02em)
- **OpenType features:** `blwf`, `cv03`, `cv04`, `cv09`, `cv11`, `tnum`, `zero`
- **Role:** Weight 400 at 72px is the signature. The hero is large and quiet, and compression comes from tracking rather than from boldness. Conventional SaaS sets heroes at 600 or 700. Duna gets its density from -0.06em tracking, which pulls letters into a single carved shape. The body steps (16, 20, 24) move on a Major Third of 1.25, then jump 1.64× from 44px to 72px, so display sizes stand apart from reading sizes. Weight 500 appears only on the 80px numerals with `tnum` and `zero`, which tells you the figures are evidence, not decoration.

### Inter — embedded widget face, outside the brand voice · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 400, Roboto at 400, Arimo at 400
- **Weights:** 400, 700
- **Sizes:** 14px
- **Line height:** 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at 14px
- **Role:** Inter appears twice, at 14px in a third-party consent and utility layer. It is a system intruder, not a brand choice. Keep it out of marketing surfaces so that GT America stays the only voice.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | GT America | 400 | 12px | 1.3 | 0.24px | `--text-small` |
| caption | GT America | 400 | 13px | 1.4 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | GT America | 400 | 14px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | GT America | 400 | 16px | 1.5 | -0.16px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | GT America | 400 | 20px | 1.4 | -0.4px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | GT America | 400 | 24px | 1.4 | -0.72px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | GT America | 400 | 40px | 1.2 | -1.2px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | GT America | 400 | 44px | 1.1 | -2.2px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | GT America | 400 | 72px | 1.0 | -4.32px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | GT America | 500 | 80px | 1.0 | 0px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline from 40px to 72px in GT America weight 400 with tracking between -0.03em and -0.06em. Restraint at display size is non-negotiable, and it is the system's thesis.
- Reserve weight 500 for the 80px stat numerals with `tnum` and `zero`. The single weight step tells readers that a number is evidence.
- Use #160f0c on every filled action with a 999px radius. One CTA color in one shape makes "Schedule a demo" impossible to miss without any saturation.
- Keep saturated color in the paintings and gradient fields, and limit UI hue to 6px dots in #45848d or #aeec1d. The interface stays ink-on-paper while the art supplies warmth.
- Build containers by tonal step: #ffffff canvas, #f7f7f5 quote panels, #edece7 cards at 24px radius. Surface shifts replace borders and shadows.
- Separate editorial content with 1px #edece7 hairlines and 128px section gaps. Air and rules structure the page the way a printed annual report does.
- Tint headline ink toward #1b0624 rather than neutral black. The plum undertone ties the type to the dusk palette of the hero painting.

### Don't

- Don't bold the H1 to 600 or 700 because "enterprise heroes need weight." At 72px with -4.32px tracking, extra weight clots the counters and turns quiet authority into a shout, which breaks the weight-400 thesis.
- Don't fill buttons with #45848d to "add brand color." Teal is a 6px status dot, and promoting it to a fill doubles the chromatic budget and makes the CTA compete with the painting.
- Don't add borders to #edece7 cards. A 1px outline on a 24px-radius tonal card reads as a form field and defeats the tonal-layering elevation model.
- Don't apply the md shadow to static cards. It belongs only to chips floating over imagery at #ffffffe6, and spreading it makes the flat paper page look like a stacked app.
- Don't use the hero's -4.32px tracking on 16px body copy. Body text sits at -0.16px, and display tracking at reading size collides letters and costs legibility.
- Don't render customer logos in their brand colors in the marquee. Full-color marks inject a dozen unbudgeted hues next to the #aeec1d signal, which must stay the brightest UI pixel.
- Don't round buttons to 8px to match the consent dialog. That widget is a vendor outlier, and a brand action should never leave the 999px pill.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- card surface: #edece7 (Stone Surface)
- quote surface: #f7f7f5 (Linen Surface)
- headline text: #1b0624 (Plum Ink)
- body text: #292421 (Graphite Ink)
- secondary text: #4d4846 (Ash Caption)
- status dot: #45848d (Lagoon Pulse)
- primary action: #160f0c (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and bars use Plum Ink #1b0624 for the primary series and Stone Surface #edece7 for the baseline, with Lagoon Pulse #45848d permitted only as a single highlighted series at 100% or as a 20% tint fill, so the data layer stays quieter than the painted imagery.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button: a pill with background #160f0c, text #ffffff, border-radius 999px, padding 12px 24px, height 48px, font GT America (fallback Inter Tight) at 20px weight 400, letter-spacing -0.4px, no border, no shadow. On hover, lighten the fill to #292421 over 150ms. Label: "Schedule a demo". Make a compact header variant at 16px with padding 8px 16px and height 40px.

2. Build a hero section: a full-bleed painted landscape image, 900px tall, its bottom 240px fading to #ffffff through a linear gradient. Overlay a transparent nav 80px tall: logo left, four 16px weight-400 links in #292421 with 32px gaps centered, and the compact pill right. Center a stack inside an 800px column. The badge comes first: background #1b062499, text #ffffff at 13px, radius 999px, padding 4px 12px. Then add 24px of space and a two-line H1 at 72px weight 400, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -4.32px, color #292421. Then add 24px and a 20px lede in #4d4846 at line-height 1.4, max-width 640px. Then add 40px and the primary pill.

3. Build a stat row: three left-aligned blocks with 48px column gaps inside a 1120px container on #ffffff. Each block is a number at GT America 80px weight 500, line-height 1.0, color #000000, with `font-feature-settings: "tnum", "zero"`, followed by 16px of space and a 16px weight-400 label in #1b0624. Above the row, place a 44px weight-400 H2 in #1b0624 at letter-spacing -2.2px and line-height 1.1, with 48px of space below it.

4. Build a floating capability tag: background #ffffffe6, border-radius 999px, padding 4px 10px, shadow `rgba(45,32,50,0.08) 0 0.6px 1.8px -0.67px, rgba(45,32,50,0.09) 0 2.29px 6.87px -1.33px, rgba(45,32,50,0.12) 0 10px 30px -2px`. Inside, place a 6px circle in #45848d, a 6px gap, and a 12px weight-400 label in #1b0624 at letter-spacing 0.24px. Scatter four tags absolutely over a blurred teal-and-ochre gradient band.

5. Build a product card: background #edece7, border-radius 24px, padding 40px, no border, no shadow. Use a 24px weight-400 heading in #1b0624 at letter-spacing -0.72px, 16px of space, 16px body in #4d4846 at line-height 1.5, then 24px of space and an inner media tile on #ffffff at 16px radius with the inset ring `rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0 0 0 1px inset`.

**Role:** The single conversion action, everywhere

Here the button carries authority through contrast alone, so the dark lozenge is the one solid shape against a painted sky.

### Pill Button — Nav Compact
**Role:** Persistent demo entry in header

The primary pill at header scale. Background #160f0c, text #ffffff, border-radius 999px, padding 8px 16px, height 40px (estimated), GT America at 16px weight 400 with -0.16px tracking, no shadow, pinned to the right edge of the navigation. It repeats the hero CTA verbatim, a deliberate redundancy: "Schedule a demo" is the only action the marketing site asks for, so the header and hero say it identically.

**Role:** Low-priority action on dark imagery

The inverted twin. Background #ffffff, text measured at #0d0d0d (not a system token; build it with Jet Figure #000000), no border, border-radius 999px, padding 12px 24px, GT America at 16px weight 400, no shadow. Use it only where the ground is painted or dark, because on the white canvas a white pill vanishes. It sits on imagery the way a mat sits under a print.

### Top Navigation Bar — Transparent
**Role:** Wayfinding floating over the painting

Chromeless and transparent. No background fill, no border and no shadow sit over the hero painting. The asterisk-and-wordmark logo is left, four text links (Product, Solutions, Company, Resources) are centered in #292421 at GT America 16px weight 400 with -0.16px tracking and 32px gaps (estimated), and the compact Ember pill is right. Height is 80px (estimated). Most B2B navs sit on a filled white bar, and dropping the bar lets the landscape run to the top edge of the viewport.

### Announcement Badge — Plum Veil
**Role:** Proof-point teaser above hero headline

A translucent stat lozenge. Background #1b062499, text #ffffff at GT America 13px weight 400, border-radius 999px, padding 4px 12px, a trailing 8px chevron, no shadow, centered 24px above the H1 and reading "seQura: 16.3x faster KYB reviews." The 60% plum lets the painted meadow tint the badge, so it belongs to the image rather than floating on top of it, a proof point delivered quietly.

### Logo Marquee Row
**Role:** Social proof in grayscale

A monochrome, auto-scrolling strip. A 13px caption in #898683 sits centered above a single row of six to seven customer logos (moss, Plaid, Svea, Mews, Brand New Day, pennylane, Qonto, Stripe, Remote), all rendered in a uniform light grey, with 64px gaps (estimated), edge-faded, on #ffffff and inside a 1120px column. Desaturating partner marks keeps the chromatic budget intact, so no customer's brand color competes with the two system dots.

### Stat Figure Block
**Role:** Outcome numbers as evidence

The system's only bold moment. The figure is GT America at 80px weight 500, line-height 1.0, color #000000, with OpenType `tnum` and `zero`, above a 16px weight-400 label in #1b0624 with a 16px gap. Three blocks sit left-aligned in a row with 48px column gaps (estimated). Weight 500 at 80px is the deliberate outlier in a weight-400 system, and it is permitted because these are measured outcomes (10.6x, 4.8x, 37%), so the type earns weight only when it reports data.

### Feature Column — Hairline Divided
**Role:** Three-up value propositions

Open columns, not boxes. A 24px line icon drawn in a 1.5px stroke (estimated) in #1b0624 sits above a 20px weight-400 title in #1b0624 and a 16px description in #4d4846 at line-height 1.5, with 24px between icon and title. The three columns are separated by 1px vertical rules in #edece7 and topped by a full-width horizontal rule. There is no fill, no radius and no shadow. Separation by hairline rather than card reads as an editorial table of contents rather than a feature grid.

### Testimonial Card — Split
**Role:** Customer quote with portrait

A two-pane quote slab. The left pane is #f7f7f5 with a 24px weight-400 quote in #292421 at -0.72px tracking and 40px padding, and the attribution sits at the bottom: name 16px #292421, title 16px #4d4846. The right pane holds a studio portrait on a warm grey backdrop measured at #dfdcd5 (decorative, not a system token). The outer border-radius is 8px, no shadow. The 8px corner is a flagged outlier against 24px cards, chosen so the photo reads as a cropped print rather than a rounded app tile.

### Product Card — Stone
**Role:** Main content container for modules

The main content card and the workhorse container (24px radius, 38 measured uses). Background #edece7, no border, border-radius 24px, padding 40px, inner tiles at 16px radius on #ffffff or #f7f7f5, headings at GT America 24px weight 400 in #1b0624, body 16px in #4d4846, no shadow. Tonal layering does the work that shadows do elsewhere. Warm stone sitting on white is the elevation, which keeps the page flat and paper-like.

### Floating Capability Tag — Frosted
**Role:** Feature labels over gradient fields

Small glass chips scattered over the blurred teal-and-ochre field. Background #ffffffe6, text #1b0624 at GT America 12px weight 400 with +0.24px tracking, a 6px #45848d leading dot, border-radius 999px, padding 4px 10px, shadow md. These are the only shadowed elements in the system, because they float over a painting with no tonal ground to separate them. The variant "Built for the AI era" chip swaps the dot to #aeec1d and the fill to #ffffff1a (glass tint, not a system token), text #ffffff.

### Consent Dialog Buttons — System Outlier
**Role:** Third-party cookie accept/reject

Embedded widget controls that break the system's own rules. Reject is #eeeeee with #444444 text, and Accept is #000000 with #ffffff text. Neither #eeeeee nor #444444 is a system token. Both use border-radius 8px, padding 10px, height 34px, a generic sans at 14px weight 400, no shadow. They are square-ish where every brand action is a pill. The deviation is allowed only because the widget is vendor-owned. Do not copy this 8px button into brand surfaces.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline from 40px to 72px in GT America weight 400 with tracking between -0.03em and -0.06em. Restraint at display size is non-negotiable, and it is the system's thesis.
- Reserve weight 500 for the 80px stat numerals with `tnum` and `zero`. The single weight step tells readers that a number is evidence.
- Use #160f0c on every filled action with a 999px radius. One CTA color in one shape makes "Schedule a demo" impossible to miss without any saturation.
- Keep saturated color in the paintings and gradient fields, and limit UI hue to 6px dots in #45848d or #aeec1d. The interface stays ink-on-paper while the art supplies warmth.
- Build containers by tonal step: #ffffff canvas, #f7f7f5 quote panels, #edece7 cards at 24px radius. Surface shifts replace borders and shadows.
- Separate editorial content with 1px #edece7 hairlines and 128px section gaps. Air and rules structure the page the way a printed annual report does.
- Tint headline ink toward #1b0624 rather than neutral black. The plum undertone ties the type to the dusk palette of the hero painting.

### Don't

- Don't bold the H1 to 600 or 700 because "enterprise heroes need weight." At 72px with -4.32px tracking, extra weight clots the counters and turns quiet authority into a shout, which breaks the weight-400 thesis.
- Don't fill buttons with #45848d to "add brand color." Teal is a 6px status dot, and promoting it to a fill doubles the chromatic budget and makes the CTA compete with the painting.
- Don't add borders to #edece7 cards. A 1px outline on a 24px-radius tonal card reads as a form field and defeats the tonal-layering elevation model.
- Don't apply the md shadow to static cards. It belongs only to chips floating over imagery at #ffffffe6, and spreading it makes the flat paper page look like a stacked app.
- Don't use the hero's -4.32px tracking on 16px body copy. Body text sits at -0.16px, and display tracking at reading size collides letters and costs legibility.
- Don't render customer logos in their brand colors in the marquee. Full-color marks inject a dozen unbudgeted hues next to the #aeec1d signal, which must stay the brightest UI pixel.
- Don't round buttons to 8px to match the consent dialog. That widget is a vendor outlier, and a brand action should never leave the 999px pill.

## Surfaces

| Level | Name | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | Page body, stat rows, feature columns, logo marquee |
| 1 | Linen Surface | `#f7f7f5` | Testimonial quote panes and quiet inset blocks |
| 2 | Stone Surface | `#edece7` | Product cards at 24px radius and hairline dividers |
| 3 | Frosted Glass | `#ffffffe6` | Chips and tags floating over painted or gradient imagery |
| 4 | Ember Ink | `#160f0c` | Inverted surface for every primary action pill |

## Elevation

- **Floating capability tags over gradient fields:** `rgba(45, 32, 50, 0.08) 0px 0.6px 1.8px -0.67px, rgba(45, 32, 50, 0.09) 0px 2.29px 6.87px -1.33px, rgba(45, 32, 50, 0.12) 0px 10px 30px -2px`
- **Inset tiles and image frames needing a defined edge on white:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 0px 0px 1px inset`

Two shadows exist on a 102,873px-tall page, so the default elevation model is tonal layering. Note that the layered shadow is tinted rgb(45, 32, 50), a plum, rather than neutral black, which keeps even the system's one drop shadow in the aubergine family of #1b0624.

## Imagery

Imagery is painterly illustration. Soft oil-or-gouache landscapes of mountains, lakes, meadows and wildflowers under peach-and-lilac skies fill the hero edge to edge, then dissolve into the white canvas through a feathered bottom fade instead of a hard crop. A second register is the blurred, grainy teal-and-ochre gradient field behind the "AI agents that follow your policy" band. It is a decorative backdrop, not a system token. Photography is limited to studio portraits in testimonials, shot against warm grey and framed by the card's 8px radius with no shadow. Product images and media sit at 24px radius. Icons are monoline outlines at 24px in #1b0624. The narrative is pastoral calm laid over regulatory machinery: compliance rendered as open landscape rather than a control room.

## Layout

Content holds a 1200px maximum with a 1120px working column. Narrow 800px and 640px measures center headlines and ledes. Sections breathe on a 128px rhythm, from 64px to 140px. The hero is a full-bleed painting with the nav floating transparently on top: logo left, four links centered, Ember pill right, height 80px (estimated). A centered stack follows of badge, 72px two-line H1, 20px lede in #4d4846 and pill CTA, all sitting in the faded lower third of the image. Sections alternate between white editorial bands (stats in three columns, features in three hairline-divided columns, a single-row logo marquee of six to seven marks) and full-bleed imagery bands. The testimonial splits at roughly 4:3. The footer is a quiet multi-column link block on white. At 375px, set the H1 at 40px, use 64px section gaps and stack every grid to one column. Density: spacious.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- card surface: #edece7 (Stone Surface)
- quote surface: #f7f7f5 (Linen Surface)
- headline text: #1b0624 (Plum Ink)
- body text: #292421 (Graphite Ink)
- secondary text: #4d4846 (Ash Caption)
- status dot: #45848d (Lagoon Pulse)
- primary action: #160f0c (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and bars use Plum Ink #1b0624 for the primary series and Stone Surface #edece7 for the baseline, with Lagoon Pulse #45848d permitted only as a single highlighted series at 100% or as a 20% tint fill, so the data layer stays quieter than the painted imagery.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button: a pill with background #160f0c, text #ffffff, border-radius 999px, padding 12px 24px, height 48px, font GT America (fallback Inter Tight) at 20px weight 400, letter-spacing -0.4px, no border, no shadow. On hover, lighten the fill to #292421 over 150ms. Label: "Schedule a demo". Make a compact header variant at 16px with padding 8px 16px and height 40px.

2. Build a hero section: a full-bleed painted landscape image, 900px tall, its bottom 240px fading to #ffffff through a linear gradient. Overlay a transparent nav 80px tall: logo left, four 16px weight-400 links in #292421 with 32px gaps centered, and the compact pill right. Center a stack inside an 800px column. The badge comes first: background #1b062499, text #ffffff at 13px, radius 999px, padding 4px 12px. Then add 24px of space and a two-line H1 at 72px weight 400, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -4.32px, color #292421. Then add 24px and a 20px lede in #4d4846 at line-height 1.4, max-width 640px. Then add 40px and the primary pill.

3. Build a stat row: three left-aligned blocks with 48px column gaps inside a 1120px container on #ffffff. Each block is a number at GT America 80px weight 500, line-height 1.0, color #000000, with `font-feature-settings: "tnum", "zero"`, followed by 16px of space and a 16px weight-400 label in #1b0624. Above the row, place a 44px weight-400 H2 in #1b0624 at letter-spacing -2.2px and line-height 1.1, with 48px of space below it.

4. Build a floating capability tag: background #ffffffe6, border-radius 999px, padding 4px 10px, shadow `rgba(45,32,50,0.08) 0 0.6px 1.8px -0.67px, rgba(45,32,50,0.09) 0 2.29px 6.87px -1.33px, rgba(45,32,50,0.12) 0 10px 30px -2px`. Inside, place a 6px circle in #45848d, a 6px gap, and a 12px weight-400 label in #1b0624 at letter-spacing 0.24px. Scatter four tags absolutely over a blurred teal-and-ochre gradient band.

5. Build a product card: background #edece7, border-radius 24px, padding 40px, no border, no shadow. Use a 24px weight-400 heading in #1b0624 at letter-spacing -0.72px, 16px of space, 16px body in #4d4846 at line-height 1.5, then 24px of space and an inner media tile on #ffffff at 16px radius with the inset ring `rgba(0,0,0,0.05) 0 0 0 1px inset`.

## Weight Restraint

The discipline is that one family at one weight carries every level of hierarchy. GT America at weight 400 spans 12px captions to the 72px hero, and differentiation comes from size jumps (1.25 at body scale, 1.64 from 44px to 72px) and from tracking that tightens in proportion to size, from -0.01em at 16px to -0.06em at 72px. Three things break it: setting H2s at 600 "for scannability", introducing a second display family, or letting the medium cut leak into body copy. To extend the system, add new levels by size and tracking only. A new 56px tier gets -0.05em and weight 400, and weight 500 stays locked to tabular numerals that report measured outcomes.

## Pigment Quarantine

All saturated color is quarantined inside imagery. The hero painting, the blurred gradient bands and the portrait backdrops supply peach, lilac, ochre and teal, while the UI layer spends exactly two hues on 6px dots: #45848d on capability tags and #aeec1d on one signal chip. Three things break the quarantine: a teal button, a lime underline on links, or full-color customer logos, because each moves pigment from the frame onto the wall. To extend the system, put new emotional color into new paintings or gradient fields, and give new UI states their meaning through tonal surfaces (#f7f7f5, #edece7) or Plum Ink #1b0624 rather than a fresh hue. Anything functional stays ink, stone or paper.

## Similar Brands

- **Duna** — Shares with Mercury the painterly landscape imagery set behind a restrained single-grotesk interface, though Duna's illustration is warmer and pastel where Mercury's runs cooler and darker.
- **Duna** — Shares with Anthropic the warm off-white canvas tones and the quarantine of color into illustration, with Duna using GT America at 400 where Anthropic pairs a serif with its sans.
- **Duna** — Shares with Persona the KYC/KYB category and a light theme, but swaps Persona's product-screenshot-led heroes for fine-art landscapes and a single ink pill.
- **Duna** — Shares with Vanta compliance positioning and stat-row proof points, differing in its weight-400 headlines where Vanta sets heavier, tighter display type over saturated purple.
- **Duna** — Shares with Linear the dense negative tracking on display headlines (-0.05em class), applied on a white paper canvas rather than Linear's dark graphite.
